concepts.label: node
concepts.gloss: A node is a forwarding element that belongs to a topology and hosts termination points and links.
concepts.example: R1 is a node in the topology 'the OTN-over-optical domain' (t.topo).

concepts.label: link-termination-point
concepts.gloss: A link-termination-point is a termination point on a node where a link ends and attaches.
concepts.example: nep-R1-R2 is a link-termination-point on node R1 that terminates the link link-R1-R2.

concepts.label: transitional-link
concepts.gloss: A transitional-link (adaptation link) is an adaptation connection at a node that connects to a layer-protocol-qualifier.
concepts.example: OTU4/ODU2 adaptation at R1 is a transitional-link at node R1 that adapts to the layer-protocol-qualifier 'ODU2 mapped into OTU4'.

concepts.label: service-interface-point
concepts.gloss: A service-interface-point is an access point on a node that provides access to a connectivity-service.
concepts.example: sip-A1-odu is a SIP on node A1 that accesses connectivity-service cs-a1a3-odu2.

concepts.label: connectivity-service
concepts.gloss: A connectivity-service is a service realized over a topology by using SIPs and CEPs; it represents a customer-facing connection through the network.
concepts.example: cs-a1a3-odu2 (ODU2, A1 to A3) is a connectivity-service that uses sip and is realized by cep-a1a3-R1 within the topology.

concepts.label: layer-protocol-qualifier
concepts.gloss: A layer-protocol-qualifier is a multiplex that qualifies a connectivity-service by mapping one layer protocol to another within the topology.
concepts.example: ODU2 mapped into OTU4 qualifies the connectivity-service cs.

concepts.label: node-rule-group
concepts.gloss: A node-rule-group is a grouping of switching rules on a specific node used to implement cross-connect behavior.
concepts.example: R2 cross-connect rule group is a node-rule-group on node R2.

concepts.label: link
concepts.gloss: A link is a connection between two nodes that is terminated by link-termination-points on its ends.
concepts.example: link-R1-R2 is a link between node R1 and R2 terminated by nep-R1-R2.

concepts.label: topology
concepts.gloss: A topology is a collection that contains nodes and links forming a multi-layer network domain.
concepts.example: the OTN-over-optical domain is a topology containing the nodes R1, R2, R3, A1, A2, A3 and the links such as link-R1-R2.

concepts.label: connection-end-point
concepts.gloss: A connection-end-point is an endpoint on a node that is part of a connectivity-service, serving as one end of a realization of the service.
concepts.example: cep-a1a3-R1 is a connection-end-point on node R1 that is part of connectivity-service cs-a1a3-odu2.
